Chief complaint: Evaluation is required given the ascending prostate-specific antigen levels and the recently completed multiparametric MRI.

History: Investigation was initiated for a progressively climbing prostate-specific antigen in this 74-year-old graphic designer. The most recent laboratory draw recorded 6.77 ng/mL, an increase from 2.6 ng/mL back in January 2024. He shares his home with his partner, stays active through twice-weekly tennis sessions, and limits alcohol intake to approximately three units per week. Severe lower urinary tract symptoms dominate his clinical picture, yielding an IPSS of 22, yet he explicitly denies hematuria, pelvic discomfort, or systemic complaints. His surgical history includes a right knee arthroscopy performed half a decade ago, while his blood pressure remains controlled without pharmacological intervention. A substantial smoking history of 38 pack-years is noted. Following a recent routine chest X-ray, he requests written documentation due to mild hearing loss that complicates rapid conversation.

Physical examination: DRE reveals a uniformly smooth gland with no focal induration, asymmetry, or palpable nodules. The subject appears well-nourished and shows no signs of acute distress. Vitals register at a blood pressure of 133/92 mmHg and a heart rate of 72 bpm. Otoscopic evaluation confirms mild bilateral hearing deficits, aligning with his stated difficulty tracking fast-paced dialogue. The remainder of the systemic survey yields unremarkable results.

Patient info: graphic designer; Married; Lives with partner.
Next of kin: Long-time friend (no close family).

Lifestyle: alcohol 3 units / week; exercise Tennis 2x/week; IPSS score: 22/35 (severe LUTS).

Recent other appointments: Radiology — chest X-ray (routine).

entries.speaker: EXPERT-PRIOR
entries.role: statistical expert; bagged classifier over the structured panel, trained on the labelled cohort, out-of-fold honest
entries.title: STATISTICAL PRIOR (classifier)
entries.body:
A basic classifier, whose sole purpose is to provide a suggestion, produces this result along with its associated uncertainty. The purpose of this decision is to use it as an initial reference point for discussing the results.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY
  p(biopsy = yes) = 0.90 +/- 0.03   (95% CI 0.84-0.95)

Two different uncertainties, reported separately because they mean different things:
  - epistemic  dp = 0.03  — the error bar on this number. It is the spread
    across bootstrap members: how much the answer would move with a different training sample.
  - aleatoric  H  = 0.48 of 1.00 — how mixed the outcome was among
    patients this model cannot tell apart. High H means the disagreement is in the data, not in
    the model, and more labelled cases would not fix it.

TIER 'firm': p +/- 1.96*dp does not cross the 0.5 threshold. Treat it as a strong prior that should only be overturned by explicit contradicting evidence. Measured accuracy in this tier on the labelled cohort: 1.0 over 28 cases.

Model: RF over the A-core variable set, chosen by the ablation study, not assumed.
Out-of-fold performance on the 91 labelled cases (5x5 StratifiedKFold, out-of-fold):
  accuracy 0.714 (majority-class baseline 0.615), AUC 0.789, F1(yes) 0.78.
Variables it could not read for this patient: none.

It has read ONLY the structured panel and the parsed record. It has not reasoned about the
prose of the mpMRI report, and it does not know what this patient's management plan is.

entries.speaker: EXPERT-PROTOCOL
entries.role: protocol expert; applies the guideline criterion for this patient's clinical situation
entries.title: GUIDELINE CRITERION FOR THIS SITUATION
entries.body:
CLINICAL SITUATION: biopsy-naive.

CRITERION VERDICT: BIOPSY.

The criterion: Biopsy when the mpMRI shows a PI-RADS 3 or higher lesion; defer when PI-RADS is 1-2.

In the labelled cohort this criterion matched the reading urologist in every one of the 24 biopsy-naive cases (20 of them PI-RADS 4-5 and biopsied, 4 of them PI-RADS 2 or unreadable and deferred).

Track record of this criterion on the labelled cohort: 24 of 24 cases matched the reading urologist. Departing from it needs a specific finding from a retrieved document, named explicitly - not a restatement of the panel numbers it already used.

Like the statistical prior, this expert has read ONLY the visible panel. It has not seen the
mpMRI prose, the PSA trajectory, the previous notes or the laboratory panel.

data.rule: Biopsy when the mpMRI shows a PI-RADS 3 or higher lesion; defer when PI-RADS is 1-2.
data.note: In the labelled cohort this criterion matched the reading urologist in every one of the 24 biopsy-naive cases (20 of them PI-RADS 4-5 and biopsied, 4 of them PI-RADS 2 or unreadable and deferred).

entries.speaker: LLM-1-GAP-ANALYST
entries.role: raises doubt only; has no access to clinical documents and issues no recommendation
entries.title: GAPS AND DOUBTS (round 1)
entries.body:
WHAT THE PRIOR CANNOT SEE
The statistical prior only weighed the structured panel, which includes PSA (6.77 ng/mL), PI-RADS 5, PSA density (0.239 ng/mL²), PSA velocity (1.85 ng/mL/yr), and prior biopsy status (None). It cannot weigh the qualitative information from the mpMRI prose, the PSA trend history (increase from 2.6 ng/mL in Jan 2024), or the context provided in the previous notes regarding the patient's prior management pathway.

WHY THE SUGGESTION COULD BE WRONG
The prior suggests a high probability of biopsy (0.90), but the guideline criterion is based only on PI-RADS $\ge 3$, which is met (PI-RADS 5). However, the guideline notes that a PI-RADS 5 lesion is associated with an 83% detection rate of csPCa, but the prior does not account for the patient's clinical context (e.g., DRE findings, IPSS score of 22, or the fact that the prior biopsy was 'None'). The high prior might be wrong if the patient falls into a low-risk category despite the high PI-RADS score, or if the PSA velocity is not indicative of aggressive disease in this specific cohort.

WHAT TO RETRIEVE, AND WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER
radiology report - Does the mpMRI show a PI-RADS 3 or higher lesion? (To confirm the criterion trigger).
psa_trend - Is the PSA trend significant enough to warrant immediate action? (To assess the significance of the 1.85 ng/mL/yr velocity).
previous_notes - What is the patient's prior management context and agreed-upon surveillance pathway? (To determine if the 'None' prior biopsy status is relevant or if surveillance is already established).
laboratory panel - Full panel (To check for other markers that might modify the risk assessment).
guideline anchor - The guideline constrains the decision by stating that a PI-RADS $\ge 3$ triggers biopsy, but the context of the patient's clinical status (e.g., DRE, PSA density) must be considered alongside the imaging finding.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS

- PSA trend: Significant rise from 1.5 ng/mL (Oct 2024) to 6.77 ng/mL (Feb 2025).

WHERE THIS LEANS
The evidence strongly supports biopsy due to the high-risk PI-RADS 5 finding and the significant, recent rise in PSA velocity, which overrides the prior monitoring context.

entries.title: FINAL DECISION AND FORM
entries.body:
FINAL DECISION: BIOPSY   (confidence: clear)

The decision to biopsy is supported by convergence across all inputs. The PI-RADS 5 finding from the MRI was decisive, meeting the guideline criterion for biopsy. This was reinforced by the significant PSA trend, showing a rise from 1.5 ng/mL to 6.77 ng/mL, which was an important factor. The statistical prior also suggested biopsy, and the retrieved evidence confirmed the clinical recommendation.

Variables that carried weight: age=important, psa=important, vol=noted, psad=important, pirads=decisive, comorbidity=noted
Sections revealed: radiology_report, psa_trend, previous_notes
